_how: The words and numbers of the workbench page. Edit this file, then run: node hub/build.mjs && node hub/check.mjs
Every line is meant to be read in a glance: keep bullets under about 12 words.
steps[].state is done, running or next. pictures[].src is a path from the portage folder, or a path inside the site (shots/...).
title: Portage
subtitle: The workbench: every step so far

steps.title: The rules
steps.asked: A survival crafting game where you start with a canoe.
built: 12 main quests, 8 side quests
Hunger, thirst, energy, storms, capsizing
Crafting, 4 hulls, 19 attachments
Runs with no screen at all
proof: A bot plays from first bail to the Beacon

steps.title: A playable grey-box, with sound
steps.asked: It needs a nice lobby screen and menu with settings and everything.
built: The whole game in plain grey shapes
Lobby, saves, settings, every key rebindable
Every sound made in code
proof: 367 tests, 10 browser tests pressing real keys
snags: Nobody has listened to the sound yet

steps.title: Three looks to choose from
built: A Cutbank, B Ink & Wash, C Blue Hour
Same scene in each, scored on six points
proof: Scores: 50, 50 and 45 out of 60
You picked B

steps.title: B2: the look made sharp and still
steps.asked: The weird moving/rippling effect... it's making me sick.
built: The moving line effect is off for good
Draws at the screen's full size
More pen detail inside the washes
proof: 0 land pixels move with a still camera
Sharp at 1080p, 1440p and 4K
You picked B2

steps.title: The look and the menus in the real game
built: The real game drawn in B2
Ink & Wash lobby, menus and HUD
proof: 477 tests, 31 browser tests
The bot finishes the game in the new look
snags: A frame-rate test failed on a busy Mac. Rule changed, then break-tested

steps.title: A player that never goes blurry
steps.asked: The player should never derender or go blurry.
built: Crew and canoe always drawn at full size
Picture quality climbs back after a slow spell
A far-away player gets a finer pen
proof: Found the cause: the whole picture shrank to 62%
Player keeps 96 to 99% of its sharpness
snags: The game did not get faster

pictures.alt: A far-away player, before and after

steps.title: Rules for a crew of four
steps.asked: Is this possible to do co-op? 4 players at once?
built: Up to 4 players, one shared canoe
Tools belong to the whole crew
F is the action key, the lantern is L
Scavenging takes one press
proof: Solo plays the identical game on six seeds
Old saves still load
snags: One press did not shorten the game: 106 to 110 minutes

steps.title: Item icons
steps.asked: Icons make it easy to remember.
built: 54 drawn icons, one per item
Shown in every panel that names an item
proof: Removing one drawing fails 6 checks
snags: Five may not read well: bellows, lodestone, spruce gum, roast roots, dried apple

steps.title: The crew, drawn properly
built: Each player in their own seat and colours
Paddling, bailing, sleeping and walking for themselves
proof: Two players' screens match pixel for pixel
A drifting canoe shows nobody paddling

steps.title: The canoe
steps.asked: A crazy impressive canoe with other things on it.
built: 4 hull tiers you can tell apart
All 19 attachments, drawn for this hull
Odile, Wren and Tink as their own figures
proof: 24 checks, each seen to fail when broken
60 fps fully fitted with four aboard
snags: The starting canoe is now grey, not red: your call
The hull's floor is drawn 5 cm shallow
Kneelers' paddles cross the outrigger decks

steps.title: The valley
steps.asked: Scavenge islands for stock food and tools.
built: Every landmark: steeple, silos, pylons, bridge, dam
All 22 scavenge node types
15 islands, each known by its outline
proof: 0 land pixels move at four islands
21% fewer triangles to draw
snags: Cabin roofs and the scrap stack are weak
Nobody has watched it in motion

steps.title: A HUD for the crew
built: Crew list: colour, place, three small meters
Crewmates on the compass and the map
Notes for everyone: who made which tool
proof: Solo HUD is the same pixels as before
snags: A pixel test failed 1 run in 4: the graphics chip, not the game
